audit.whatIsWrong: CROSS-LAYER CHART DISAGREEMENT on all seven rows. The full layer reads "Skill" on every row; the content layer reads "Aurora" on every row. The page renders two different answers to who wins each stage.
audit.why: Aurora is the correct side and two independent sources say so: packet.levelChart is all-Aurora, and the content whys argue it (whys[0] "hold the 900 and level 1 is yours", whys[1] "his taunt only reaches 275", whys[6] "the fight is about whether his knock-up finds you before your Q does"). The range facts back it: Aurora's Q is 900 against Winds of War at 825, Justice Punch needs 650, and Shield of Durand only taunts inside 275, so Galio cannot start anything from where Aurora fights. audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (a) Colossal Smash's auto-attack reset is never mentioned anywhere on the page — flagged in missingInteractions. (b) spikes[0].text contains a flat factual error: it says "Galio has almost no wave clear or poke before 6", which the kit and the page's own early paragraph both contradict, and then refers to "his passive shield timing" — Galio's passive is Colossal Smash, an empowered area auto-attack, and carries no shield at all. The shield is on W and R.
audit.why: Winds of War is an 825-range tornado dealing damage over time on an 11s cooldown; it is real poke and real waveclear, which is exactly what breakdown.early already says. Telling the reader the opposite in spikes[0] is a contradiction inside one matchup. Attributing a shield to the passive is a fabricated mechanic. The chain that actually decides the lane is stated correctly elsewhere and I verified it: Justice Punch charges 650 and knocks up the first champion it meets, and that knock-up is the only thing that delivers a 275-range taunt.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text rewritten around the real Winds of War numbers and the Justice Punch timer; breakdown.early now carries the Colossal Smash wind-up as the burst tell.
